title: Kuma Kuma Kuma Bear
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Fifteen-year-old Yuna, a shut-in who funds herself on the stock market, is sent by the game's god-like administrator into the world of her favourite VR game, wearing an embarrassing but overpowered bear suit. She hunts monsters, befriends ten-year-old Fina and her family, funds an orphanage and opens restaurants, and exposes corrupt officials, finding her new life fuller than the empty one she left (Wikipedia).
life_message: Strength and wealth are best used to look after children, friends and the vulnerable.

content.note: Monster hunting (wolves, a Black Viper), a mage's monster army defeated (Wikipedia).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Yuna answers bullying adventurers personally, but crooks are handed to lords for arrest (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Yuna lives as she pleases but works within lords' rule.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Found family with Fina plus care for a whole orphanage.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Good nobles and a king; Yuna befriends both commoners and royals.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Thrift and work for poor families, plus Yuna's own comfortable choices.

folkways.japan: The hikikomori backstory and isekai escape reflect Japanese web-novel conventions; Yuna's frugality and quiet service echo common Japanese norms.

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia premise: Yuna finds her new life more fulfilling through her actions; no reviews on delivery (to verify).
delivery.note: Kindness is shown through Yuna's deeds; greedy officials are simple villains rather than voices for a view.

winners_losers: Yuna, Fina's family, the orphans and honest lords such as Cliff win; embezzlers and greedy guildmasters (Enz Roland, Zarrad) are arrested. Generous use of power gets the sympathy (Wikipedia).
